title: The Infirmary on the Kit
lede: Plan H, your pick, built in 3D from the kit's pieces and walkable in the game. Now shows what waits on you (decisions, tasks to acknowledge or check), what is in flight and what is Claude's to do; Pieces follows every model from its picture to the scene; the area tabs hold each round's work.

decisions.title: Have a look: birches, wisteria, shrubs and fields
decisions.html:
The four foliage tasks you agreed to (top: before, below: after, in the same order: birch, wisteria, shrub, fields):

  1. Birches have bark now: chalk white with dark horizontal marks, darker at the foot, and a few dark limbs climbing into a looser crown.
  2. The wisteria hangs: a wide, low crown with long lilac and white bunches hanging from its underside, instead of a round ball of blossom. Best seen from low (third picture).
  3. Shrubs get loose sprigs past their outline and less even masses, so they read as leafy rather than as round lobes. This also changes the courtyard's bushes (gold, lilac and pink are shared); it's one setting to keep the court as it was.
  4. The fields sit on flat earth with a ragged, rounded outline instead of a raised slab with straight edges; the rows start and stop unevenly, and the wheat ripens unevenly into olive, so it's less bright.

figures.cap: Before: birch, wisteria, shrub, fields
After: birch, wisteria (low), shrub, fields
2: the wisteria from low
2: the wisteria at the game camera

decisions.rec: My view: all four are clearly better; the court's bushes gain from the sprigs too, so I would keep them shared.

decisions.title: Have a look: the beach meets the sea; vines in the purifier bay
decisions.html:
Two polish tasks you agreed to:

  1. No sea wall on the beach. The sea sat 1 m below the sand, so the map put a retaining wall with a balustrade along the water. The sea is now level with the beach: the sand runs straight into the foam. The jetty stands just above the water on its posts, without its rail. Does the jetty want its rail back, or is it right as a low landing stage?
  2. Vines in the purifier bay. It now gets its own denser vine pass, so its cliff tops carry the same flowering fringe as the cove's sides. Vines hanging all the way down a cliff face don't work yet: the rock model stands up to 1.7 m proud of the edge, so a hanging vine disappears inside it. Fixing that means fitting each vine to the rock's surface. Is it worth doing, or is the fringe along the top enough?

figures.cap: 1: the cove, sand into the sea
1: the west end of the beach
2: the purifier bay, vines along the tops
Before: the balustrade along the water

decisions.rec: My view: the beach is right as it is; the fringe is enough for now. Vines down the rock are worth doing later for every cliff at once, not just here.
decisions.closed: good (the user, in the terminal): the jetty stays a low landing stage, the fringe is enough; vines down rock faces filed as #32

decisions.title: Have a look: the beds out in front, one rune circle per junction
decisions.html:
Your two notes on the last look, done:

  1. The tents stand back from their beds. The cots were part of the tent model, so I split them out: the canopy is now its own piece, moved back about 1.7 m, and the four cots stay where they were, so they stand out in front with their pillows and emitters in view. The two north tents moved half a cell forward so their beds sit on the paving. Is that far enough back, or should the canopy go further or less?
  2. The overlapping circles were where the tent branches met the shared lines half a cell from the lines' own corners. They meet at the corner now, so there is one circle each.

decisions.rec: My view: the beds read far better; 1.7 m looks right to me.
decisions.closed: good (the user, in the terminal: "Looks good")

decisions.title: Have a look: the healing devices, the triage camp and the crystal
decisions.html:
First, your note: stretchers, crates and blankets lay across the rune lines. They are all moved clear (the stretchers now in front of their tents), and the map compiler now warns whenever a line runs through any prop, so it can't creep back. Then four things I'd like your eye on, all in the scene now:

  1. Emitters beside the pillows, not behind them. The tent model's cots run right up to its back posts, so behind the pillow they stood outside the tent under the roof, unseen. Beside each cot's head they show between the cots. I think this keeps your idea; does it?
  2. The stations stand at each tent's end where its line arrives, 1.26 m tall. Big enough to read as the thing the line feeds, or should they be larger?
  3. The triage props: 16 round the six tents (tables, stools, chests, trays, washstands, cloak stands, a lantern post), the middle round the well kept open. Right amount, or should the camp look busier?
  4. The crystal, from your answer: dull grey glass while the vines choke it, lighting up as they are cut, most at the last cuts.

A note with what to change is enough; each point becomes its own task.

decisions.rec: My view: all four work as they are; the stations could go a little larger if they read small to you.
decisions.closed: changes: tents back so the beds show (canopy and cots now separate pieces), the rune junctions joined into one circle; the rest good

decisions.title: Spend the credits on the healing devices (and the triage sheet)?
decisions.html: Codex redrew your picks as clean model references: the station with its leads snipped (the ribs end in feet on the base plate; the tent's glyph line does the wiring, so nothing comes out at 45°), and the emitter alone. Meshy 7.1 over the API: about 30 credits each, 60 for both. The triage sheet b (already OK'd) goes through meshy.ai in Chrome for the free retries, about 35 credits, and its download needs you to click Chrome's download bubble. Until then the scene has grey stand-ins in their places (Building and props tab, round 9). The permission check won't let me spend credits on a pick alone, so this asks plainly. Credits left: about 1,134, expiring 2026-12-16.

log.html: The road out reads as one band of paving since the grass merge (its weathering no longer eats the stones). The four road lamps stood as bare stand-in poles: hand-placed pieces never had their parts picked, so compile.py now picks one of each, seeded by the piece's id.

log.html: New options in foliage.ts: a birch's bark texture and limbs, spread, squash and hang on trees (the wisteria), sprigs on bushes; fields' soil a ragged flat patch (kit-render.ts), ragged row ends, an uneven wheat. Asked in rv-4.
